prompt.context: A large national zoo is considering the acquisition of a rare giant panda.
prompt.question: How would you help the zoo's management decide whether this is a worthwhile venture?

clarifying_info.q: How many visitors does the zoo currently get each year?
clarifying_info.a: 600,000 people per year — half adults, half children.

clarifying_info.q: What is the current admission price?
What has been the attendance impact at other zoos that acquired pandas?
clarifying_info.a: San Diego saw a 12% increase in overall attendance in the first year, and maintained that increase going forward.

clarifying_info.q: What are the costs of acquiring the panda?
clarifying_info.a: Acquisition fee $590,000 (immediate); new enclosure $1,475,000 (immediate); transportation $335,000 (immediate); annual panda expenditure and enclosure maintenance $300,000 per year (end of each year). Note: $200,000 in consultant fees have already been incurred.

clarifying_info.q: What discount rate should we use?
Should we assume the attendance gain is permanent?
clarifying_info.a: Yes — assume the gain experienced in the first year is maintained in perpetuity. Ignore capital maintenance or growth for simplicity.

framework: Acquisition feasibility: space/capacity/facilities, required expertise and trainers, climate/environment fit, mating arrangements and future additions
Cost impact: upfront acquisition fee and construction, ongoing annual panda expenditure and maintenance
Revenue impact: increase in visitor attendance (volume), potential premium/extra admission fee, new programs/events/shows
Financial viability: NPV of the project — compare PV of incremental annual cash flows against upfront investment, treating sunk costs correctly

questions.prompt: Identify the key issues the zoo must consider before deciding to acquire the panda.
questions.guidance: Strong answers cover three buckets: (1) Acquisition logistics — space, facilities, trainers, diet, climate/temperature, mating arrangements; (2) Cost impact — facilities build-out, training, food, ongoing maintenance; (3) Revenue impact — attendance uplift, possible premium pricing, new programming. Candidate should not jump straight to the numbers without first surfacing the qualitative considerations.

questions.prompt: Calculate whether the acquisition is financially viable using NPV.
questions.guidance: Candidate must identify the $200,000 consultant fee as a sunk cost and exclude it. Upfront costs are $590k + $1,475k + $335k = $2.4 million. Incremental revenue = 12% attendance uplift on 600,000 = 72,000 new visitors (36,000 adults + 36,000 children), yielding $900,000 in additional revenue. Net annual gain = $900,000 - $300,000 = $600,000. Perpetuity value discounted at 20% = $600,000 / 0.20 = $3 million, which must then be discounted one period: $3,000,000 / 1.20 = $2.5 million. NPV = -$2.4M + $2.5M = +$100,000. Conclusion: NPV is just positive.

math.setup: Sunk cost excluded. Upfront outlay = $590,000 + $1,475,000 + $335,000. Incremental annual visitors = 12% x 600,000, split 50/50 adults/children. Annual incremental revenue = (36,000 x $15) + (36,000 x $10). Net annual gain = incremental revenue - annual maintenance. Perpetuity PV = net annual gain / discount rate, discounted one period.

brainstorming.prompt: What factors beyond the financial calculation should the zoo consider before making its final decision?

categories.name: Acquisition logistics
ideas: Available space and whether the enclosure can be built on-site
Climate and temperature compatibility with panda habitat requirements
Availability of qualified panda trainers and veterinary expertise
Dietary requirements and reliable food supply chain
Regulatory and government permits for exotic species acquisition

categories.name: Ongoing operations
ideas: Long-term panda health and veterinary care costs
Mating arrangements and potential for additional pandas in the future
Staff training and retention for specialized animal care
International agreements or loan conditions from the panda's origin country

categories.name: Revenue upside beyond attendance
ideas: Premium or separate panda exhibit admission fee
Educational programs, school events, and corporate events
Media coverage and PR value driving broader brand awareness

categories.name: Risk factors
ideas: Attendance uplift may be lower than the San Diego benchmark
NPV is marginally positive — small cost overruns could make it negative
Panda health risks could curtail the exhibit
Reputational risk if the panda does not thrive in captivity

recommendation: The NPV is positive at +$100,000, providing a financial basis for proceeding with the acquisition
Subject to confirming the zoo has adequate facilities, expertise, and climate conditions, the acquisition is recommended
risks: NPV is only marginally positive; any cost overrun or attendance shortfall below 12% would make the project value-destructive
The 12% attendance lift is based on a single comparable (San Diego) and may not generalize to all markets
Annual maintenance costs and panda health care may increase over time
next_steps: Conduct facility and climate assessment to confirm enclosure feasibility
Benchmark attendance uplift estimates against additional zoo comparables beyond San Diego
Model downside scenarios (e.g., 8–10% attendance lift) to test sensitivity
Confirm regulatory requirements and panda loan/acquisition terms
